# 🧱 mBlock beginner examples: Ranger 2-Way

[🔙 Back to the Ranger 2-Way product page](/en/sensors/tof2/index.md)

This page is for people who have **never written a program**: read the Ranger 2-Way on an **mBot** with mBlock 5 blocks. The 5 examples start with "turn the number into a sound" and work up to a robot that drives itself. Every example has a block picture, a downloadable project file and an Arduino sketch that does the same thing.

| Software | Who it suits | How to open the example file |
|---|---|---|
| 🟧 **mBlock 5 desktop** (blocks, Upload mode) + **MBC Pro Sensors extension v2** | Schools, first time with an mBot | Download the `.mblock` → open mBlock 5 → "File → Open from your computer" → switch to "Upload" at the bottom right → "Upload" |
| 🔧 **Arduino IDE** (text code) | People who want to see what is behind the blocks, or write their own code | Download the `.ino` → install the Makeblock and MBC_Sensors libraries (see [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md)) → board Arduino Uno → upload |

> [!IMPORTANT]
> - The sensor must be the **Makeblock edition with the 2026-10 protocol v2 firmware**, connected through the **mBot socket board** to an RJ25 port; use extension **v2.0.0** (old firmware goes with the old v1 extension; they cannot be mixed).
> - The board is the **mBot (mCore)**. mBot Ranger, Orion and MegaPi work too: swap "when mBot starts up" for that board's hat block and use a port that board allows (see [supported boards and ports](/en/makeblock.md)); the mBot2 (CyberPi) has no RJ25 port and is not supported.
> - mBlock 5 is shown here with its English block text; your copy may show the same blocks in another language.

## Before you start

<figure class="ref-fig"><img src="/images/figures/tof2/wiring-mbot.svg" alt="Ranger 2-Way × mBot wiring" loading="lazy"></figure>

Sensor → mBot socket board → RJ25 port on the board (S1 = host TX, S2 = host RX, UART 38400).

1. **Install the extension**: get the **MBC Pro Sensors v2.0.0** `.mext` from [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md) and drop it into the mBlock 5 window; add **mBot** under "Devices" (bottom left) and switch to "Upload" (bottom right).
2. **Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3** (every example on this page uses this port; to use another, change the port number on the blocks).
3. **Let it boot first**: every example starts with "wait 1 seconds" so the sensor can boot; reading too early gives -32768 (nothing received yet).
4. The Ranger 2-way needs no calibration. Each laser looks straight ahead; **seen from behind the robot**, the left one is "left distance"; anything beyond 120 cm reads **120**.

## Blocks used on this page

Each reporter block is one "value id" of the sensor's value table (the same ids as the Arduino I2C registers); the full block list is in [Makeblock extension](/en/makeblock.md).

| Block | Returns | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| Ranger 2 port [3] nearer distance cm | 0~120 cm | the smaller of left and right, 0~120 cm |
| Ranger 2 port [3] left distance cm | 0~120 cm | distance from the left sensor, 0~120 cm (left = sensor 0 seen from behind the robot); 120 = nothing in range / sensor failed |
| Ranger 2 port [3] right distance cm | 0~120 cm | distance from the right sensor, 0~120 cm (right = sensor 1); 120 = nothing in range / sensor failed |

**Examples on this page**

1. [Distance theremin](#example-1-distance-theremin)
2. [Traffic-light distance warning](#example-2-traffic-light-distance-warning)
3. [Distance drives one wheel](#example-3-distance-drives-one-wheel)
4. [Drive and stop at the wall](#example-4-drive-and-stop-at-the-wall)
5. [Turn away from the nearer side](#example-5-turn-away-from-the-nearer-side)

> [!NOTE]
> The `.mblock` files are generated in the mBlock 5 save format and **have not yet been opened in mBlock 5 for verification** (pending the extension v2 release). If one will not open or shows blank blocks, check that extension v2 is loaded and the device is mBot, or rebuild it from the block picture below (under 5 minutes); you can also [tell us on LINE](https://line.me/R/ti/p/@692vcvuk).

## Example 1: Distance theremin

**What this example does**: The mBot has no screen, so this example turns the "nearer distance" (0 to 120 cm) into a pitch: the closer your hand, the lower the note; the further, the higher. Learn to "read the number" first.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- Ranger 2-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex01_theremin.mblock](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex01_theremin.mblock) | [ex01_theremin.ino](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex01_theremin/ex01_theremin.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (1) seconds
forever
  play tone ((200) + ((Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) * (10))) Hz for (0.1) seconds :: sound
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 2-Way × mBlock 5  Example 1: Distance theremin  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(1000);   // Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    buzzer.tone((200 + (mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) * 10)), 100);   // Pitch = 200 + nearer distance × 10 Hz, for 0.1 s
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
2. Repeat forever
   - Pitch = 200 + nearer distance × 10 Hz, for 0.1 s

**What you should see**: Hand 10 cm in front: a low 300 Hz; move it away and the pitch rises; nothing in front (120) is a high 1400 Hz.

**FAQ**
- **No sound?** → The buzzer is on the board and is not loud; listen closely, or change 0.1 s to 0.3 s.
- **Nothing ahead but the value is not 120?** → The laser sees the floor or table: mount it higher or tilt it slightly up. Anything beyond 120 cm reads 120.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 2: Traffic-light distance warning

**What this example does**: Use "if… then… else…" to split the distance into three bands: within 15 cm red, within 40 cm yellow, further green. This is the decision skeleton for "stop at the wall" later.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- Ranger 2-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex02_led_warning.mblock](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex02_led_warning.mblock) | [ex02_led_warning.ino](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex02_led_warning/ex02_led_warning.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (1) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (15)&gt; then
    LED [all v] colour red (255) green (0) blue (0) :: looks
  else
    if &lt;(Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (40)&gt; then
      LED [all v] colour red (255) green (255) blue (0) :: looks
    else
      LED [all v] colour red (0) green (255) blue (0) :: looks
    end
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 2-Way × mBlock 5  Example 2: Traffic-light distance warning  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(1000);   // Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) < 15)) {   // If the nearer distance is less than 15
      rgbled.setColor(0, 255, 0, 0); rgbled.show();   // Within 15 cm: red
    } else {
      if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) < 40)) {   // Otherwise, if the nearer distance is less than 40
        rgbled.setColor(0, 255, 255, 0); rgbled.show();   // Within 40 cm: yellow
      } else {
        rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 255, 0); rgbled.show();   // Further: green
      }
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearer distance is less than 15
      - Within 15 cm: red
      - otherwise:
         - Otherwise, if the nearer distance is less than 40
            - Within 40 cm: yellow
            - otherwise:
               - Further: green

**What you should see**: Bring your hand slowly closer: green → yellow (40 cm) → red (15 cm).

**FAQ**
- **Nothing ahead but the value is not 120?** → The laser sees the floor or table: mount it higher or tilt it slightly up. Anything beyond 120 cm reads 120.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 3: Distance drives one wheel

**What this example does**: Use "nearer distance × 0.8" directly as the left wheel power: the more open the front, the faster the wheel; the closer an object, the slower; right in front it stops. Prop the robot up to watch one wheel react, then drive it in the next example.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 2-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A wall or a box as an obstacle

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex03_one_wheel.mblock](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex03_one_wheel.mblock) | [ex03_one_wheel.ino](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex03_one_wheel/ex03_one_wheel.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (1) seconds
forever
  left wheel power ((Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) * (0.8)) %, right wheel power (0) % :: motion
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(1000);   // Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    wheels((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) * 0.8), 0);   // Left wheel power = nearer distance × 0.8 (0 to 96), right wheel 0
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
2. Repeat forever
   - Left wheel power = nearer distance × 0.8 (0 to 96), right wheel 0

**What you should see**: Nothing ahead: the left wheel runs at full speed. Bring your hand closer and it slows; right in front it stops.

**FAQ**
- **Nothing ahead but the value is not 120?** → The laser sees the floor or table: mount it higher or tilt it slightly up. Anything beyond 120 cm reads 120.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).

## Example 4: Drive and stop at the wall

**What this example does**: The robot drives forward and stops when the nearer distance is below 20 cm; remove the obstacle and it drives on. The most basic "sensor + if + motor" combination.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 2-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A wall or a box as an obstacle

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex04_stop_wall.mblock](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex04_stop_wall.mblock) | [ex04_stop_wall.ino](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex04_stop_wall/ex04_stop_wall.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (1) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &gt; (20)&gt; then
    left wheel power (40) %, right wheel power (40) % :: motion
  else
    stop moving :: motion
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp
// Ranger 2-Way × mBlock 5  Example 4: Drive and stop at the wall  (equivalent Arduino sketch for mBot)
// Wiring: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot port 3. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.
// Does exactly what the mBlock block example does, for people who want to see "what is behind the blocks" or use the Arduino IDE.
// Libraries needed:
//   1. Makeblock (Arduino IDE Library Manager, search "Makeblock", or the copy inside the mBlock 5 install folder)
//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(1000);   // Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) > 20)) {   // If the nearer distance is greater than 20
      wheels(40, 40);   // Clear ahead: both wheels 40, forward
    } else {
      wheels(0, 0);   // Too close: stop
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearer distance is greater than 20
      - Clear ahead: both wheels 40, forward
      - otherwise:
         - Too close: stop

**What you should see**: The robot drives forward and stops about 20 cm from the wall; it also stops for your hand and continues when you remove it.

**FAQ**
- **It bumps the wall before stopping?** → Too fast to brake: lower 40 to 30, or raise 20 to 30.
- **The robot turns the wrong way and gets worse?** → Swap the "+" and "−" (or swap the left and right wheel powers). The mBot ships with the left wheel on M1 and the right on M2; check your own wiring.
- **Nothing ahead but the value is not 120?** → The laser sees the floor or table: mount it higher or tilt it slightly up. Anything beyond 120 cm reads 120.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.

## Example 5: Turn away from the nearer side

**What this example does**: Two lasers tell you whether the obstacle is on the left or the right. When something is within 20 cm, compare left and right: nearer on the left → turn right, nearer on the right → turn left (red LED); nothing ahead → drive straight (green). A self-driving obstacle avoider.

**What you need**
- mBot (mCore board) + mBlock 5 desktop
- mBot two-wheel robot (left wheel on M1, right wheel on M2, as shipped)
- Ranger 2-Way (Makeblock edition) + mBot socket board
- A wall or a box as an obstacle

**Wiring**: Ranger → mBot socket board → mBot **port 3**. Mount it on the front with both lasers facing forward.

**Download**

| mBlock 5 project | Equivalent Arduino sketch |
|---|---|
| [ex05_avoid.mblock](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex05_avoid.mblock) | [ex05_avoid.ino](/examples/tof2/mblock/ex05_avoid/ex05_avoid.ino) |

<details open>
<summary>🧱 mBlock blocks (just rebuild them like this)</summary>

<pre class="blocks">when mBot starts up :: events hat
wait (1) seconds
forever
  if &lt;(Ranger 2 port [3 v] nearer distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (20)&gt; then
    LED [all v] colour red (255) green (0) blue (0) :: looks
    if &lt;(Ranger 2 port [3 v] left distance cm :: #0A9E8F) &lt; (Ranger 2 port [3 v] right distance cm :: #0A9E8F)&gt; then
      left wheel power (40) %, right wheel power (-40) % :: motion
    else
      left wheel power (-40) %, right wheel power (40) % :: motion
    end
  else
    LED [all v] colour red (0) green (255) blue (0) :: looks
    left wheel power (40) %, right wheel power (40) % :: motion
  end
end</pre>

</details>

<details>
<summary>🔧 Equivalent Arduino sketch (mBot)</summary>

```cpp

//   2. MBC_Sensors v2: the four files in src/ of the extension .mext (MBC_Sensors.h/.cpp, mbc_proto.h, mbc_ids.h),
//      put them in Documents/Arduino/libraries/MBC_Sensors/ and #include <MBC_Sensors.h> (https://mbc-pro-sensors.github.io/en/makeblock.html)
// Board: Arduino Uno (the mBot mCore is an Uno). After uploading, unplug USB and run on battery.

#include <MeMCore.h>            // mBot (mCore): motors, LED, buzzer
#include <SoftwareSerial.h>
#include <MBC_Sensors.h>        // MBC sensors v2 (the same library the mBlock extension uses)

MBCPort mbc_port3(3);           // sensor on mBot port 3
MeDCMotor motorL(9);           // left wheel (M1)
MeDCMotor motorR(10);          // right wheel (M2)
MeRGBLed rgbled(7, 2);         // on-board RGB LED (2 pixels)
MeBuzzer buzzer;               // on-board buzzer

// left / right wheel power -100~100 (positive = forward): the mBot left wheel is mounted mirrored, so M1 gets the negative value; % becomes PWM 0~255
void wheels(int l, int r) {
  l = constrain(l, -100, 100); r = constrain(r, -100, 100);
  motorL.run(-l * 255 / 100);
  motorR.run(r * 255 / 100);
}

void setup() {   // everything runs inside setup(), just like the program mBlock generates
  mbc_port3.begin();
  delay(1000);   // Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
  while (1) {   // Repeat forever
    if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x03) < 20)) {   // If the nearer distance is less than 20
      rgbled.setColor(0, 255, 0, 0); rgbled.show();   // Obstacle: red LED
      if ((mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x01) < mbcRead(mbc_port3, 0x02))) {   // If the left distance is less than the right distance
        wheels(40, -40);   // Nearer on the left: spin right
      } else {
        wheels(-40, 40);   // Nearer on the right: spin left
      }
    } else {
      rgbled.setColor(0, 0, 255, 0); rgbled.show();   // Clear ahead: green LED
      wheels(40, 40);   // Drive straight
    }
  }
}

void loop() {}   // nothing here: the blocks above never return
```

</details>

**Step by step**
1. Wait 1 s for the sensor to boot
2. Repeat forever
   - If the nearer distance is less than 20
      - Obstacle: red LED
      - If the left distance is less than the right distance
         - Nearer on the left: spin right
         - otherwise:
            - Nearer on the right: spin left
      - otherwise:
         - Clear ahead: green LED
         - Drive straight

**What you should see**: The robot drives straight with a green LED; at an obstacle it turns red and spins toward the more open side, then drives on once the way is clear.

**FAQ**
- **Stuck spinning in a corner?** → When both sides are close it keeps flipping. Add "if the nearer distance is below 8, reverse for 0.5 s first".
- **The robot turns the wrong way and gets worse?** → Swap the "+" and "−" (or swap the left and right wheel powers). The mBot ships with the left wheel on M1 and the right on M2; check your own wiring.
- **Nothing ahead but the value is not 120?** → The laser sees the floor or table: mount it higher or tilt it slightly up. Anything beyond 120 cm reads 120.
- **Nothing happens, or the value stays at -32768?** → Wrong port (every example on this page uses port 3), socket board not seated, or the sensor is not the Makeblock edition. Check with the "MBC common → connected?" block first; "protocol version" must read 2 for the new firmware (old firmware needs extension v1).
- **Upload fails, or the blocks are blank?** → Make sure the switch at the bottom right is in "Upload" mode, extension v2 has been dropped into mBlock, and the USB cable goes to the mBot board.
